title: optimize
description: Stage output contract: one reasoned speed pass over the change (impact classification, clear local fixes with their rationale), plus the cross-cutting changes it deliberately did NOT make.

impact.description: how close the change sits to a latency-sensitive path: `hot_path` (it changes one), `local` (near one, or code where speed still matters), `none` (offline tools, docs, tests only — the pass commits nothing and stops). Optional so outputs recorded before it existed still parse; an absent value reads as unclassified, never as `none`.

changes.description: each speed fix this pass committed, with its one-line rationale (e.g. 'dict lookup instead of a list scan per row: O(N^2) -> O(N)'). Optional; empty or omitted for a no-op pass.

rationale.description: why it is faster, one line

measurements.description: what you actually timed, before and after, if you timed anything. Optional — measuring is welcome when cheap but not required to keep a change. MODEL-REPORTED profiling detail: it decides nothing; the engine runs the project adapter's declared benchmark itself and reverts only on a measured regression (see `benchmark`). Report what you ran, never an estimate.

name.description: what was measured (the benchmark/operation), not the optimization

unit.description: e.g. ms, s, ops/s, MB — state it, or before/after are unreadable

benchmark.description: ENGINE-OWNED verdict (#520) — do NOT author this key: whatever a stage returns here is overwritten by the engine's own before/after run of the project adapter's declared benchmark command, taken at the last-good checkpoint and at this stage's commit. The keep rule is NO REGRESSION, not a measured win. `status` is `verified` (measured, no comparable metric regressed past the tolerance — commit kept; `reason` is `improved` or `no_regression`), `regressed` (a metric got slower past the tolerance — reverted), `failed` (the benchmark was green at the anchor but red or unreadable at the stage's commit, i.e. the change broke it, or the tree could not be put back after measuring — reverted), `unverified` (nothing could be measured: no adapter benchmark, a benchmark already broken at the anchor, no shared metric, a dirty worktree, no anchor — commit KEPT, warning-grade) or `skipped` (the pass committed nothing, e.g. `impact: none`, so the benchmark did not run). `no_win` and `unavailable` are the pre-redesign statuses (a win was required then, and unmeasurable meant reverted); they appear only on runs recorded before the change.

impact.description: the stage's own impact classification, echoed on a skipped verdict

reverted.description: whether the engine CONFIRMED the stage's commit is off the worktree HEAD — not merely that a reset was attempted. False on a not-kept verdict means the commit may still be on the branch, `revert_unconfirmed` names why, and the stage is failed rather than reported green.

revert_unconfirmed.description: why the engine could not confirm the commit was removed; present only on a not-kept verdict whose revert it could not verify

head_unconfirmed.description: on an unverified verdict whose measurement reset failed: why the engine could not confirm the kept commit is still checked out (the stage is then failed)

tolerance.description: the noise band: a metric must move by more than this fraction to count as regressed (reverts) or improved (reported)

metrics.description: one row per metric measured on both sides: name/before/after/unit/lower_is_better/delta_fraction (signed so positive is better)/direction/judged

suggestions.description: cross-cutting or architectural changes this stage judged out of its own scope and did NOT apply (a process-pool restructure, a shared-memory layout, a different lock strategy) — so a task never turns into a redesign and the idea is not lost. Optional; omit or return an empty array when there are none. The engine files one as an enhancement issue at finalize only when it carries an explicit `file` disposition, subject to the same per-task cap and title dedupe as a review finding.

description.description: the change itself, one sentence first — its leading line becomes the enhancement issue title

rationale.description: why it would pay off, and what this pass found that points at it — the issue body

disposition.description: same filing threshold as a review finding's. Choose `file` deliberately, with justification, to open an enhancement issue; `drop` for something a maintainer would not independently prioritize. An absent or unrecognized disposition is surfaced in the completion note, never filed — filing requires explicit `file`.
